Situation 1: Expert Ltd. has depreciation amounting to ₹6,00,000 in its books as per accounting records and depreciation as per tax records at ₹15,00,000. There is adequate evidence of future profit sufficiency.

Situation 2: Further, they have accrued ₹8,00,000 towards GST liability for the last month of the year which is expected to be paid off by next month. As per the provisions of Section 43B of the Income Tax Act, 1961 – Any expenditure of the nature mentioned in section 43B (e.g. taxes, duty, cess, fees, etc.) accrued in the statement of profit and loss on mercantile basis will be allowed for tax purposes in subsequent years on payment basis only.

Answer the following questions on the basis of above information.
question_html: In Situation 1: How much deferred tax asset/liability should be recognized as transition adjustment when the tax rate is 50%:
answer_html: Answer: (ii) ₹4,50,000 (deferred tax liability) — tax depreciation (₹15,00,000) exceeds book depreciation (₹6,00,000) by ₹9,00,000, a timing difference that will reverse in later years as book depreciation catches up, so it originates a deferred tax liability: ₹9,00,000 × 50% = ₹4,50,000.

case_facts_html:
Situation 1: Expert Ltd. has depreciation amounting to ₹6,00,000 in its books as per accounting records and depreciation as per tax records at ₹15,00,000. There is adequate evidence of future profit sufficiency.

Situation 2: Further, they have accrued ₹8,00,000 towards GST liability for the last month of the year which is expected to be paid off by next month. As per the provisions of Section 43B of the Income Tax Act, 1961 – Any expenditure of the nature mentioned in section 43B (e.g. taxes, duty, cess, fees, etc.) accrued in the statement of profit and loss on mercantile basis will be allowed for tax purposes in subsequent years on payment basis only.

Answer the following questions on the basis of above information.
question_html: In Situation 2: How much deferred tax asset/liability should be recognized as transition adjustment when the tax rate is 35%:
answer_html: Answer: (i) ₹2,80,000 — the case narrative's own stated rule is that Section 43B expenditure accrued on a mercantile basis is allowed for tax purposes only in a subsequent year, on payment basis. The ₹8,00,000 GST liability is therefore fully disallowed for tax this year (added back to taxable income) even though it is expensed in the books, making taxable income higher than accounting income this year – a deductible timing difference that reverses (and becomes tax-deductible) in the following year when actually paid. This originates a deferred tax asset: ₹8,00,000 × 35% = ₹2,80,000.

case_facts_html:
The following particulars are stated in the Balance Sheet of Star Limited as on 31st March, 2023: Deferred Tax Assets (Dr.) ₹1,20,000; Deferred Tax Liabilities (Cr.) ₹2,10,000.

The following transactions were reported during the year 2023-24: (1) Depreciation as per accounting records ₹12,00,000. (2) Depreciation as per income tax records ₹18,00,000. (3) Interest paid accounted in books on accrual basis ₹4,50,000 but paid on 15-05-2024. (4) Employer PF Contribution exp. disallowed for tax purpose ₹82,000 in year 2022-23 but allowed in year 2023-24. (5) Unamortized preliminary expenses as per tax records ₹1,00,000. (6) Donation ₹70,000. (7) Tax Rate 20%.

Based on the information given in above Case Scenario, answer the following Question No. 5-8.
question_html: What would be the value of the Deferred Tax Assets as on 31-03-2024?
answer_html: Answer: (C) ₹1,23,600. Opening DTA ₹1,20,000, less reversal of last year's PF-contribution-disallowance DTA (₹82,000 × 20% = ₹16,400, since the amount disallowed in 2022-23 is now allowed in 2023-24), plus a new DTA on the unamortized preliminary expenses still to be claimed for tax (₹1,00,000 × 20% = ₹20,000). The interest accrued in books but paid on 15-05-2024 creates no timing difference: since it was paid before the due date of filing the return of income, Section 43B's proviso allows it as a deduction in the year of accrual itself, so no DTA arises on this item. Net: ₹1,20,000 − ₹16,400 + ₹20,000 = ₹1,23,600.

topic_text: AS 22 (4.5): Measurement of deferred tax assets - timing differences reversing/originating, and the Sec 43B proviso exception for interest paid before the return-filing due date

question_html: What would be the value of the Deferred Tax Liabilities as on 31-03-2024?
answer_html: Answer: (B) ₹3,30,000. Opening DTL ₹2,10,000, plus a new DTL on the depreciation timing difference: tax depreciation (₹18,00,000) exceeds book depreciation (₹12,00,000) by ₹6,00,000, taxed-benefit-now-reversing-later × 20% = ₹1,20,000. Closing DTL = ₹2,10,000 + ₹1,20,000 = ₹3,30,000.

case_facts_html:
The following particulars are stated in the Balance Sheet of Star Limited as on 31st March, 2023: Deferred Tax Assets (Dr.) ₹1,20,000; Deferred Tax Liabilities (Cr.) ₹2,10,000.

The following transactions were reported during the year 2023-24: (1) Depreciation as per accounting records ₹12,00,000. (2) Depreciation as per income tax records ₹18,00,000. (3) Interest paid accounted in books on accrual basis ₹4,50,000 but paid on 15-05-2024. (4) Employer PF Contribution exp. disallowed for tax purpose ₹82,000 in year 2022-23 but allowed in year 2023-24. (5) Unamortized preliminary expenses as per tax records ₹1,00,000. (6) Donation ₹70,000. (7) Tax Rate 20%.

Based on the information given in above Case Scenario, answer the following Question No. 5-8.
question_html: Which is the permanent difference item as per AS 22?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Donation — disallowed for tax purposes permanently under the Income-tax Act, with no future reversal, unlike the other three items (PF contribution, preliminary expenses, depreciation) which are all timing differences that reverse in a later period.

case_facts_html:
V Limited contracted to construct a hostel for MR College at ₹224 lakhs on 1st October, 2024 (expected completion 18 months). Cost incurred to 31st March, 2025: ₹60 lakhs. Prudent estimate of additional cost for completion: ₹180 lakhs. Billed to MR College: ₹84 lakhs.

On 1st June, 2024, V Limited acquired 30% of M Limited for ₹20,00,000, gaining significant influence. On 14th August, 2024, M Limited declared a dividend of ₹5,00,000 out of its FY2023-24 profit of ₹8,00,000. M Limited earned ₹30,00,000 for FY2024-25 (profits accrue evenly) and declared a dividend of ₹6,00,000 on 15th June, 2025.

V Limited's pre-tax profit: Q1 FY2024-25 ₹7,00,000, Q2 ₹8,00,000, expected Q3 ₹4,00,000, Q4 ₹6,00,000. Corporate tax slab: 30% on first ₹5,00,000, 40% on additional earnings.

Deferred tax information as at 31st March, 2025: Depreciation per accounting records ₹4,00,000; Depreciation allowable under Section 32 of the Income Tax Act ₹10,00,000; Unamortized Preliminary Expenses per tax records ₹30,000; GST penalty imposed 30th March, 2025, payable 30th April, 2025, ₹1,25,000.

Based on the information given above, answer Question Nos. 6–9.
question_html: Assuming a tax rate of 30%, determine the amount of Deferred Tax Asset/Liability as at 31st March, 2025. There is adequate evidence of future profit sufficiency.
answer_html: Answer: (A) DTL ₹1,71,000 — net timing difference: depreciation (₹10,00,000 tax vs ₹4,00,000 book, a ₹6,00,000 taxable timing difference) less unamortised preliminary expenses (₹30,000 deductible timing difference); the GST penalty is not a timing difference (a permanent difference, not deductible for tax at all) and is excluded. Net ₹5,70,000 × 30% = ₹1,71,000 DTL.
chapter_label: AS 22: Accounting for Taxes on Income
topic_text: AS 22 (4.4): Deferred tax on timing differences - depreciation and preliminary expenses; a penalty is a permanent difference, excluded
